steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import multiple named exports from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The import statement for React and useState is added, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: import statement
from 'react'
React
useState
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Check that you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package using the correct syntax.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import React and useState from the 'react' package using an import statement.

steps.title: Create the main component function
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ToggleVisibility that returns JSX.Element. Use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a function component that returns JSX.Element. You can use 'function ToggleVisibility(): JSX.Element { ... }' or 'const ToggleVisibility = (): JSX.Element => { ... }'.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ToggleVisibility component function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ToggleVisibility is defined with proper TypeScript typing, ready to contain the toggle logic and UI.
successCriteria: The component is named ToggleVisibility, returns JSX.Element, and is syntactically valid TypeScript/TSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ToggleVisibility component with proper TypeScript typing.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the component is named exactly 'ToggleVisibility' and returns JSX.Element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incorrect. Create a function component named ToggleVisibility that returns JSX.Element.

steps.title: Initialize the visibility state
steps.instruction: Inside your ToggleVisibility component, declare a state variable called isVisible using the useState hook, initializing it to false. Use TypeScript to type it as boolean.
steps.hint: The useState hook returns an array with two elements: the current state value and a setter function. Use array destructuring to assign them to isVisible and setIsVisible.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a boolean state variable
const [isVisible, setIsVisible] = useState<boolean>(false);
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a boolean state variable isVisible initialized to false, ready to track whether content should be shown or hidden.
successCriteria: The code must include a useState call with <boolean> type parameter, destructured into isVisible and setIsVisible, initialized to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the isVisible state variable with useState. This boolean will control whether content is visible or hidden.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with <boolean> type, destructuring into isVisible and setIsVisible, and initializing to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to declare a state variable called isVisible using useState, typed as boolean and initialized to false.

steps.title: Define the toggle handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your component, define a function named handleToggle that will toggle the isVisible state when called. Use the setter function from useState to update the state.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setIsVisible with the opposite of the current isVisible value. You can use the previous state to calculate the new value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleToggle function is defined inside the component that properly toggles the isVisible state.
successCriteria: The code should contain a function named handleToggle that calls setIsVisible to toggle the boolean state value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the toggle handler function. This function will be called later to change the visibility state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but the handler might not toggle the state correctly. Make sure handleToggle uses setIsVisible to change isVisible to its opposite value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle handler function isn't defined correctly. You need to create a function named handleToggle that calls setIsVisible to toggle the isVisible state.

steps.title: Start the component return statement
steps.instruction: Add a return statement to your component that returns a parent <div> element.
steps.hint:
Inside your component function, add 'return (
);' to start the JSX structure.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX structure starting with a parent <div> element.
successCriteria: The component must include a return statement that returns a JSX element (starting with <div>).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've started the JSX structure with a return statement and a parent div element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a JSX element (like <div>) from your component.
steps.feedbackWrong:
The component doesn't have a proper return statement with JSX. Add 'return (

steps.title: Add the toggle button
steps.instruction: Inside the return statement's div, add a button element with an onClick handler that calls the toggleVisibility function. The button should have text like 'Toggle Visibility'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with onClick={toggleVisibility} and include descriptive text inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element is added inside the div that will trigger the toggleVisibility function when clicked.
successCriteria: button element present
onClick handler set to toggleVisibility
button contains text
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that will toggle the visibility state when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a button with an onClick handler that calls toggleVisibility and includes some text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't set up correctly. Check that you've added a button element with onClick={toggleVisibility} and text content.

steps.title: Set the button text based on state
steps.instruction: Inside your button element, set the text content to 'Show' when isVisible is false, and 'Hide' when isVisible is true using a ternary expression.
steps.hint: Use the isVisible state variable in a ternary expression like this: {isVisible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'} as the button's text content.
steps.expectedOutcome: The button will display 'Show' when the content is hidden (isVisible is false) and 'Hide' when the content is visible (isVisible is true).
successCriteria: The button element should contain a ternary expression that uses the isVisible state variable to conditionally display 'Show' or 'Hide' as text content.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional logic to dynamically change the button text based on the visibility state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the isVisible state variable in a ternary expression inside the button element to show 'Show' when false and 'Hide' when true.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button text isn't dynamically changing based on the isVisible state. Remember to use a ternary expression like {isVisible ? 'Hide' : 'Show'} inside the button element.

steps.title: Add conditional content container
steps.instruction: Add a <div> element after the button that will serve as a container for the content you'll show/hide. For now, just create the empty container.
steps.hint: Place a new <div> element right after the closing </button> tag, inside the outer <div>.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has an empty <div> container element after the button, ready to hold content that will be conditionally displayed.
successCriteria: Add a <div> element after the button
The new div should be inside the outer <div> container
The div can be empty or contain a comment placeholder
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the container that will hold our toggleable content. Next, we'll add the actual content inside it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a <div> element after the button, inside the outer <div> container.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Add a <div> element right after the button, inside the outer <div>. This will be our content container.

steps.instruction: Inside the content container div, use a conditional statement to only render content when isVisible is true. You can use a ternary operator or logical AND (&&).

successCriteria: Conditional rendering is used inside the container div

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented conditional rendering. The content will now only appear when the visibility state is true.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your conditional statement. Make sure you're using isVisible as the condition and placing the content inside the container div.
